subject: Biotechnology
title: Microbiome Engineering for Crops
description: Learn Microbiome Engineering for Crops in one minute.

hook.text: The soil teems with billions of microbes — engineering this hidden community can boost crop health dramatically.

buildup.text: Mycorrhizal fungi extend root networks — delivering phosphorus in exchange for plant sugars. Ancient symbiosis.

discovery.text: Indigo Agriculture coats seeds with beneficial microbes — improving drought tolerance and nutrient uptake naturally.

twist.text: Soil microbiomes vary wildly between fields — one farm's miracle microbe may be another farm's dud.

climax.text: Synthetic microbial consortia are designed using AI — communities of bacteria tailored to specific soil conditions.

punchline.text: Engineer the soil, not just the seed — microbiome farming is the next revolution.

quiz.question: Why don't microbial seed coatings work equally well on all farms?
options: Seeds reject foreign microbes after germination
Soil microbiomes vary between fields, and a beneficial microbe in one context may not thrive in another
Microbial coatings only work on genetically modified seeds
